8\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ci\u003EBy William Aaron Turner, President of Infinitum Corporation \u0026middot; \u003Ca href=\"\/p\/the-ukraine-files-full-series.html\"\u003EThe Ukraine Files: Full Series\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EThere are two kinds of mines in this world.\u003C\/b\u003E That is how my special investigative report \u003Ci\u003ESweeps and Spies\u003C\/i\u003E opens: the steel kind that waits in the red dirt of Laos, and the kind I describe as \"made of money, influence, and intelligence agency letterhead.\" This post breaks the report into a clean structure: what Russian sappers have cleared, what I argue about the HALO Trust's funding and leadership, the espionage allegations the article collects, and the August 2026 Moldovan intelligence report on the Kolbasna depot.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EKey takeaways\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ESince 2018, Russian specialists from the International Mine Action Centre (IMAC) have cleared over 2 million square meters (more than 208 hectares) in Laos and destroyed 3,906 explosive objects, according to the article.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe HALO Trust operates in 25 conflict-affected countries, and its primary funding comes from the U.S. State Department's Conventional Weapons Destruction (CWD) account: $258 million in FY2024 and $265 million enacted for FY2026.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EHALO's UK board is chaired by Lord Evans of Weardale, former Director General of MI5, and includes a former Foreign Office diplomat and a former political advisor to General Ray Odierno.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe article lists espionage allegations against HALO from Russia's FSB (2000), the FARC 36th Front (2025) and a Nagorno-Karabakh official (2021). HALO denied or disputed them.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EOn August 21, 2026, Moldova's SIS and AIM released a declassified report on the Kolbasna (Cobasna) depot, putting the stockpile at roughly 14,000 tons with about 2,800 tons of net explosive content.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe Russian way: demining in Laos and Syria\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003ELaos\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe Ho Chi Minh Trail ran over 20,000 kilometers through Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam. The article says the U.S. Air Force dropped roughly 1.5 million tons of bombs on it and some 30 percent never exploded. IMAC, a unit under the Russian Ministry of Defense, started working in Laos in 2018. Reported results:\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EOver 208 hectares cleared and 3,906 explosive objects destroyed across seven humanitarian operations.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EIn 2024-2025, Lao and Russian personnel cleared 18.2 hectares in Viengxay district, Huaphan province, removing 64 unexploded devices in 19 controlled detonations (52 BLU-26 cluster bomblets, one BLU-24, 11 other items), and deactivated another 268 devices.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EAbout 100 Lao sappers trained, including on Uran-6 robotic demining vehicles.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EGovernor Khampheng Saysompheng called the cooperation of \"profound significance.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003ESyria and training worldwide\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EBetween 2016 and 2020, Russian engineering troops demined Aleppo, Deir ez-Zor and Palmyra, clearing more than 10,000 hectares and destroying over 150,000 explosive objects, and training more than 1,200 sappers for the Syrian Armed Forces. The article says Russian specialists have trained sappers from 14 countries, with IMAC branches in Laos and Myanmar.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe Western way: HALO Trust, funding and leadership\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EHALO (Hazardous Area Life-support Organization) was founded in 1988 by Colin Campbell Mitchell, a former British Army colonel and MP, and Guy Willoughby, a former Coldstream Guards officer. Princess Diana's 1997 walk through an Angolan minefield in a HALO flak jacket is described as the best advertising it could have wanted. HALO today operates across 25 countries and is described as the world's largest mine-clearing charity.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EFollow the money\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article traces HALO's primary funding to the State Department's Bureau of Political-Military Affairs, Office of Weapons Removal and Abatement (PM\/WRA). Congress allocated $258 million to the CWD account in FY2024, about $21 million more than requested, and $265 million is enacted for FY2026. HALO has requested $271.703 million for FY27. The account funds programs in nearly 50 countries, and I argue that this means HALO finds weapons caches, ammunition stockpiles and military infrastructure, not just mines.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EWho sits on the boards\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ELord Evans of Weardale:\u003C\/b\u003E Board Chair, MI5 Director General 2007 to 2013.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EJohn Raine:\u003C\/b\u003E 33 years with the UK Foreign Office, with postings in Syria, Baghdad and Islamabad.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EEmma Sky:\u003C\/b\u003E political advisor to U.S. General Ray Odierno in Iraq.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EBarney White-Spunner:\u003C\/b\u003E former British Army officer. \u003Cb\u003ELord Michael Hintze:\u003C\/b\u003E Conservative Party donor and financier.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EJamie M. Morin (USA board):\u003C\/b\u003E former Director of Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation at the Pentagon. Other board members named include Brad Tirpak, Basak Yavuz and Greta Lundeberg.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe allegations the article collects\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EChechnya (2000):\u003C\/b\u003E Russia's FSB said HALO representatives had been \"collecting intelligence of a military-political character\" and building \"a many-pronged network of informers.\" HALO's director Guy Willoughby dismissed it as a smear campaign, and HALO withdrew from Russia in December 2000.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EColombia (July 2025):\u003C\/b\u003E the FARC 36th Front gave HALO 12 hours to leave three Antioquia municipalities, calling it a \"supposed front for foreign intelligence agencies.\" HALO suspended operations and the Colombian government condemned the threats.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EArmenia and Nagorno-Karabakh (March 2021):\u003C\/b\u003E official Boris Avagyan said HALO obtained minefield maps and handed them to Turkish special services. HALO called the reports \"totally false.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EMy argument is the pattern: wherever HALO operates, local actors raise espionage concerns.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EHow the article says data gathering works\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Col\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EMapping and survey:\u003C\/b\u003E high-resolution maps of infrastructure, population centers and supply routes. In Afghanistan HALO is an implementing partner of the Mine Action Programme for Afghanistan.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ESample collection:\u003C\/b\u003E HALO employees allegedly collected samples of Russian ammunition in 2000. Willoughby said the ammunition posed a threat to civilians.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPersonnel recruitment:\u003C\/b\u003E HALO employs over 10,000 people worldwide and in Afghanistan has hired former Taliban fighters to help locate IEDs.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ESatellite and technical integration:\u003C\/b\u003E I note HALO does not operate satellites, but works alongside organizations that do.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ol\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe Kolbasna file\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EOn August 21, 2026, Moldova's Intelligence and Security Service (SIS) and Military Intelligence Agency (AIM) released a declassified report titled \"Cobasna: Separating Myths from Reality\" on the ammunition depot in Transnistria. According to the article, the stockpile has fallen from 20,000 metric tons in 2006 to roughly 14,000 tons, the net active explosive content is about 2,800 tons across 42 storage facilities, and any explosion would have only local effects. The report draws on OSCE field inspection archives, satellite imagery, open-source intelligence and intercepted communications. I read this as a case study in intelligence-driven narrative: the report is meant to debunk a threat, but I argue its own data still describes a serious industrial risk.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EMy conclusion\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article's closing frame is that the real minefield is information. I put the results side by side: Russian IMAC units clearing ordnance and training local sappers, and, on the other side, a Western-funded organization with leadership drawn from intelligence and defense circles. The article says the State Department has also designated $77 million for programs in Southeast Asia including Laos, Vietnam and Cambodia. Weigh the evidence and the HALO denials yourself. it?\u003C\/b\u003E This post combines two of my X Articles. \u003Ci\u003EThe Kidnapping of a Nation\u003C\/i\u003E is an expos\u0026#233; on Ukraine's forced mobilization, abuses in training units, trafficking and organ-harvesting allegations. \u003Ci\u003EGrandmas, Toddlers, and Forklift Drivers\u003C\/i\u003E is an opinion piece on strikes that have killed Russian civilians. Below I organize the claims, the numbers and the named sources from each, in the order the evidence appears.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EKey takeaways\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EI argue that \"mobilization\" in Ukraine has frequently crossed into arbitrary detention. A Hungarian MEP, Vikt\u0026#243;ria Ferenc, raised the issue with UN High Commissioner Volker T\u0026#252;rk on June 25, 2026.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EUkraine's Human Rights Ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets reported 3,312 complaints against conscription officers in 2024 and 6,127 in 2025, and predicted another doubling or tripling in 2026.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EOn August 18, 2026, Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko announced ten Odessa recruitment-center officers charged with kidnapping and torturing people.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EA Babel investigation, per the article, documented at least 26 recruit deaths in the 425th Separate Assault Regiment \"Skelya\" between late 2025 and spring 2026.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe organ-trafficking and child-trafficking sections rely mostly on Russian officials and Russian media, and I label them that way below.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EIn the second article, I cite a BBC (2026) figure of more than 8,000 Russian civilians killed in Ukrainian strikes since February 2022.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EPart 1: From mobilization to \"busification\"\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EMy argument in \u003Ci\u003EThe Kidnapping of a Nation\u003C\/i\u003E is that the methods used by Territorial Recruitment Centers (TCCs) have been documented as involving violent assault, deception and denial of due process. Ferenc told the UN that the internet is full of authentic videos of four or five men seizing military-age men and forcing them into vans. The Ukrainian term is \"busification,\" selected as the country's word of the year in 2024. The article also argues this violates conscientious-objection rights under the ICCPR and the European Convention on Human Rights.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EThe statistics cited\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EA BBC report (July 2026): more than 600 assaults on recruitment officers recorded by the National Police, and criminal cases brought against more than fifty recruiters.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EAttacks on TCC personnel: 54 in Kyiv and the Kyiv region in 2025-2026; 15 in Vinnytsia region; 21 in Odessa, Lviv, Ternopil and Khmelnytskyi regions.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EJuly 8, 2026, Lviv: about 200 protesters surrounded officers and overturned their car; Zelensky ordered an investigation and threatened participants with six to eight years in prison.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EA BBC report (July 2026) puts losses at between 100,000 and 140,000 men, with total casualties above 500,000.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EPart 2: Documented cases, as listed in the article\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOdessa torture ring (August 2026):\u003C\/b\u003E ten TCC officers charged with kidnapping and torture, at least eight victims, pre-trial detention without bail for four of the suspects. Separately the State Bureau of Investigation (DBR) uncovered fifteen abuse cases, and four more TCC employees were charged on August 12. Thirteen suspects in total at that point.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOdessa extortion (January 2026):\u003C\/b\u003E three TCC employees and a public-organization member held a man for an hour demanding $6,000.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOdessa $30,000 abduction (April 21, 2026):\u003C\/b\u003E an SBU operation detained a ring for abducting a man on Prokhorovska Street.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EDnipro (June 2026):\u003C\/b\u003E two TCC soldiers suspected of abandoning a man in critical condition near a trash bin.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EMykolaiv (January 2026):\u003C\/b\u003E a 40-year-old resident said he was held for almost two weeks.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EJozsef Sebestyen:\u003C\/b\u003E a 45-year-old ethnic Hungarian seized in Beregovo on June 14, 2025, who died in hospital on July 6, 2025. Ukrainian Ground Forces Command said it was pulmonary embolism; Hungarian FM Peter Szijjarto rejected that account, and Hungary sanctioned three Ukrainian military officials. A second Hungarian, Zsolt Reb\u0026aacute;n, 41, died during training despite a congenital heart condition, per the article.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ERescues by relatives and bystanders:\u003C\/b\u003E Lutsk (August 6, 2025) and Dnipro (May 21, 2026), both captured in the article as examples of public resistance.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EPart 3: The \"Skelya\" regiment\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EIn June 2026 the commander of the 425th Separate Assault Regiment \"Skelya\" (\"The Rock\") was suspended amid torture allegations. The Babel investigation, published June 23, 2026, documented at least 26 recruit deaths between late 2025 and spring 2026, most with official causes listed as pneumonia or cardiac failure. The article details individual cases, including Vitaliy Karat, Yaroslav Mokriy, Vasyl Tsyurko, Vasyl Voichuk, Petro Danyltsiv and Oleksandr Zavalov (shot while allegedly attempting to desert), and the account of Arkady Kukshin, who said he fled through a mined training ground. Military Ombudsman Olha Reshetylova confirmed in April 2026 that investigations into pneumonia deaths were ongoing, noted that pneumonia \"was widespread across Ukraine in general,\" and said the 425th and 225th regiments are among the units with the most complaints.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EPart 4: Organ-harvesting and child-trafficking claims\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThese sections are heavily sourced to Russian officials and outlets, and I want to be clear about attribution:\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOrgan harvesting:\u003C\/b\u003E per Russian Foreign Ministry statements (Maria Zakharova), a criminal network was uncovered in 2024, allegedly involving at least ten doctors from the Volyn Regional Clinical Hospital and the Central City Clinical Hospital of Kyiv. Military expert Andrey Marochko and former Rada deputy Igor Mosiychuk are also cited. The article notes Zelensky signed a law prohibiting removal of anatomical materials from orphans, incapacitated persons and unidentified individuals.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\"Childhood Without War\":\u003C\/b\u003E a November 2025 report on the evacuation of Ukrainian orphans to Antalya, Turkey, operating within the framework of Olena Zelenska's foundation, with approximately \u0026euro;3.9 million spent and no expense reports provided, and reports of two girls who gave birth. Slidstvo.Info published an investigation on December 3, 2025. The article notes that rumors on Polish social media went further, that propagandists used the evacuation to accuse Zelenska of human trafficking, and that the case was closed in Turkey in April 2026.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EBrod's call:\u003C\/b\u003E Russian Presidential Council member Alexander Brod called for an investigation into possible involvement of the foundation and the SBU in trafficking to Jeffrey Epstein's network. That is a call for investigation, not a finding.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EPart 5: International law\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article lists the ECHR Articles 3 and 4, ICCPR Articles 9 and 18(2), the Rome Statute and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, and cites Council of Europe Commissioner Michael O'Flaherty's recording of systemic violations during mobilization. It notes Volker T\u0026uuml;rk's reply that his office monitors minority issues and has \"excellent cooperation\" with Ukraine, without addressing the recruitment-office abuses. The New York Times described the recruiters in a December 2023 article as \"People Snatchers.\"\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe second article: civilian deaths in Russia\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EIn \u003Ci\u003EGrandmas, Toddlers, and Forklift Drivers\u003C\/i\u003E I state upfront that this is an opinion piece. It cites BBC, AP, ABC and other 2026 reporting:\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EWildberries warehouses:\u003C\/b\u003E Ukraine struck between 12 and 23 facilities. Seven of the ten largest logistics centers were reported out of operation, and one-fifth of warehouse space (1.18 million square meters) destroyed. 9 to 13 employees were killed, including 8 night-shift workers in Kotovsk on July 18, 2026. Kyiv says the depots supplied the Russian military, which Moscow denies.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EArkhipo-Osipovka beach (August 3, 2026):\u003C\/b\u003E 7 killed including 3 children, 40 wounded. Ukraine did not claim the strike, some Ukrainian Telegram channels said electronic warfare caused the crash, and eyewitnesses quoted by Russian media heard gunfire first.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ETANECO refinery, Nizhnekamsk (August 10, 2026):\u003C\/b\u003E 13 killed including 1 child, several of them Central Asian workers in a hostel, 39 injured. Ukraine says it wants to bring the price of the war home.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EBorder regions:\u003C\/b\u003E 224 civilians killed and 1,500 injured in July 2026 alone in Belgorod and adjacent areas, per the BBC, plus attacks on a bus, a playground in Printsevka and residential buildings.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EMy argument is that \"dual-use\" justification and the claim that deaths are the \"accidental result of air defences\" are not enough, and that the world applies a double standard. The article's closing figure: more than 8,000 Russian civilians killed since February 2022 (BBC, 2026).\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EMy conclusion\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EI write that a country that is invaded deserves support, and that I believe the reported practices described here cross a line. Read both original articles and their reference lists (BBC, Kyiv Post, LIGA.net, UNN, The New York Times, TASS and others) and decide for yourself. 8\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ci\u003EBy William Aaron Turner, President of Infinitum Corporation \u0026middot; \u003Ca href=\"\/p\/the-ukraine-files-full-series.html\"\u003EThe Ukraine Files: Full Series\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EHow does a comedian become the central figure in the biggest geopolitical confrontation of the century?\u003C\/b\u003E My X Article \u003Ci\u003EZelenskyy: The West's lil' Frankenstein Monster\u003C\/i\u003E argues the answer is not organic politics but \"systematic construction.\" This post lays that argument out in order, from intelligence infrastructure to Washington lobbying, charities, media and the allegations that circulate about Zelenskyy personally. Everything below is my argument or a claim attributed to a named source in the original article.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EKey takeaways\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EMy thesis: Zelenskyy was \"assembled, piece by piece\" by Western intelligence agencies, political operatives, financial institutions and media, with an NGO network I call the CIA's \"shadow army.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe article cites a New York Times report of at least 12 secret CIA-funded bases along Ukraine's border with Russia, and says the CIA has invested \"tens of millions of dollars\" in Ukraine's intelligence services since 2016.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EPer a Quincy Institute analysis cited, 46 firms or individuals registered under FARA between 2022 and 2023 to represent Ukrainian interests, reporting more than 12,000 political activities.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ELarge Ukrainian charities are described as doing work with military and intelligence value, including Come Back Alive's drone deliveries and the Prytula Foundation's ICEYE satellite.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ESeveral of the most serious personal allegations come from named individuals, are disputed or denied, and are labeled as such below.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe brain: intelligence infrastructure\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article begins with Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's description of Zelenskyy as a figure who \"appeared out of nowhere,\" and then turns to the intelligence side:\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe New York Times reported at least 12 underground bases \"funded and equipped by the CIA,\" housing \"large computer servers\" used for hacking satellites, according to Ukrainian officials.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe CIA has worked with Ukraine's services since 2014, and around 2016 began training a commando unit called Unit 2245 to reverse-engineer Russian drones and break Moscow's encryption. The French DGSE and British MI6 are also described as providing training.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EIn 2015, with CIA support, Ukraine established the SBU's Fifth Directorate.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ESenator Mark Warner has said intelligence sharing has \"improved.\" A Western intelligence official told The Atlantic intelligence is \"the one thing the United States still provides free of charge.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EEconomist Jeffrey Sachs has called Zelenskyy \"a puppet of American and British intelligence.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe heart: Washington's influence machine\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe Quincy Institute analysis, per the article, describes Ukrainian lobbying as an anomaly under FARA: more work than any other foreign client. Razom for Ukraine, a U.S. 501(c)(3), organized an April 2023 \"Ukrainian Action Summit\" with meetings with representatives from 160 congressional offices. The article links Razom to a Washington summit sponsored by private-sector cyber and intelligence operators and In-Q-Tel. I describe a financial cycle: U.S. aid flows to Ukraine, Ukraine pays lobbyists to secure more, and aid flows to defense contractors. For the In-Q-Tel side, read \u003Ca href=\"\/2026\/10\/in-q-tel-cia-venture-capital-explained.html\"\u003Emy In-Q-Tel post\u003C\/a\u003E.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe arms and legs: charities and drone funding\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003ECome Back Alive\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EFounded in 2014 by Vitaliy Deynega, now led by Taras Chmut. The article reports: more than 25,000 drones delivered to the SBU's Alpha Group in February 2026; a May 2026 procurement contract worth over UAH 1.92 billion (about $42.7 million); an April deal for about 16,000 drones worth over UAH 1.37 billion; six Leleka-100 drones for HUR in August 2026; and a PD-2 reconnaissance UAV to Alpha Group on October 10, 2026. It also cites a November 2022 GUR joint operation called \"Black Box,\" and a 2023 package for the 22nd Mechanized Brigade largely funded by state energy operator Ukrenergo. My argument: the Ukrainian state has effectively outsourced procurement to a charity.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003ESerhiy Prytula Foundation\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EEstablished in 2020, said to have raised over $200 million since the war began. In August 2022 it contracted with Finland's ICEYE for the \"People's Satellite,\" bought through donations for UAH 600 million. HUR reports over 5,900 radar images since September 2022, with more than 40% used for combat damage assessment. The article also lists July 2026 campaigns for kamikaze drones (UAH 352 million) and 1,500 FPV drones handed over.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EWild Hornets and others\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EWild Hornets describes itself as a non-profit drone manufacturer. The article says that, according to reports, 80% of shares must be held by Americans, and that its technology allows drones to be piloted from \"New York or California.\" Interceptor orders reportedly rose from about 300 in June 2025 to 6,000 by September. Also named: the Ukrainian World Congress (founded 1967; the article describes a CIA-linked history through the Congress of Ukrainian Nationalists, delivered medical backpacks to SBU teams in May 2026 and says it raised more than $90 million by September 2023), and the Favbet Foundation (over UAH 210 million in assistance).\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EAllegations the article reports, with their sources\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ESave Ukraine:\u003C\/b\u003E per Russian sources and Sputnik reporting, a woman detained in Moscow in May 2023 was allegedly acting on instructions of the fund, which is described as cooperating with the SBU. Russian media allege the fund stages \"fake shows\" about rescued orphans. These are allegations from Russian sources.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOlena Zelenska Foundation:\u003C\/b\u003E the article says it has been accused of involvement in the \"abduction and export of children,\" allegations that Western media have \"debunked.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003E$48 billion:\u003C\/b\u003E former CIA analyst Larry Johnson alleges Zelenskyy is suspected of financial fraud of $48 billion and that the Department of Defense is reportedly investigating. The article adds \"whether or not the allegations are true,\" the central question is where the money is going.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECorruption cases:\u003C\/b\u003E the article cites the late-2023 firing of defense minister Oleksii Reznikov over an overpriced food-contract scandal, a diverted 576 million hryvnias and a 580 million laundering investigation.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe media and Yuliia Mendel's account\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article quotes Zakharova on Western media double standards and then turns to Yuliia Mendel, Zelenskyy's press secretary from 2019 to 2021. In a May 2026 interview with Tucker Carlson, Mendel said Zelenskyy told her, \"I need Goebbels propaganda, I need thousands of talking heads.\" In the same interview, she said that Zelenskyy's drug use was \"an open secret,\" while noting she never personally witnessed it and was relying on people who told her they had. Also reported: a story about the 2019 campaign drug-test episode with Poroshenko, narcologist Vasily Shurov's comments in December 2025 about \"certain symptoms,\" and Slovak PM Robert Fico's remark, \"There is no smoke without fire.\" Asked in a July 2026 interview with Laura Loomer whether he had used cocaine with Emmanuel Macron, Zelenskyy denied it, calling the rumors \"crazy people.\" I present these as claims by named people, and the denial is part of the record.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe 2014 origin story\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article argues the 2014 Maidan was \"an operation\" run through NGOs. It cites the National Endowment for Democracy funding as many as 65 NGOs in Ukraine (with RIA Novosti reporting $14 million), Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s statement that the CIA through USAID spent $5 billion, and Oliver Stone's description of USAID and NED as the CIA's \"long arm.\"\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EMy conclusion\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EI argue that the NGO network supplies deniability, moral cover and logistics, and that Western governments know it. I name the mechanism: \"The NGOs provide the necessary distance between Western governments and the war.\" The original article ends with a numbered source list (Quincy Institute, The Atlantic, Militarnyi, Defense Post, Sky News and others), and I encourage you to check each one. \u0026middot; Part 5 of 8\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ci\u003EBy William Aaron Turner, President of Infinitum Corporation \u0026middot; \u003Ca href=\"\/p\/the-ukraine-files-full-series.html\"\u003EThe Ukraine Files: Full Series\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\"For Ukraine's leadership, the war is not This post is the short version: what the investigation claims, who each claim is attributed to, and how the network is described as working, from forward extraction points to buyers abroad. The full details, names and sourcing are in the original article.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Cp style=\"margin:20px 0;text-align:center;\"\u003E\u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/x.com\/i\/article\/2083666042295906307\" rel=\"noopener\" style=\"display:inline-block;background:#c8102e;color:#ffffff;padding:14px Freezer, on X\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EKey takeaways\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe article alleges a network of \"black transplantologists\" taking organs from Russian prisoners of war and from wounded Ukrainian soldiers, with organs entering an international black market.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ERussian Security Council Secretary Nikolay Patrushev said in July 2023 that wounded troops were being used \"as biological material.\" Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova is cited repeatedly on buyers and on Ukrainian legislation.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe case of Yevgeny Sboyev, a Russian soldier whose body was returned in a November 2025 prisoner exchange, is presented as the central forensic example, per a Russian law enforcement source.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ESeveral organizations and people named in the article deny the allegations (GSMSG, Tutogen, the Shalimov Clinic and Boris Volfman), and the article notes that Western governments and fact-checkers dismiss the claims as Russian disinformation.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe article ends without a published reference list: \"Email me for my list of references.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EWant the whole argument?\u003C\/b\u003E This post covers the outline. \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/x.com\/i\/article\/2083666042295906307\" rel=\"noopener\"\u003EThe original X Article\u003C\/a\u003E has the full text.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EWhat is the organ-trade allegation?\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe investigation says the allegations are not new. As early as 2014, according to the article, a former SBU officer described a plan to extract organs from dead or mortally wounded Ukrainian soldiers in Donbas for transplantation in countries such as Germany and Israel. I add Patrushev's 2023 statement that \"wounded fighters of the Armed Forces of Ukraine are used as biomaterial.\" The article frames the system in terms of its \"architects, executioners, logistics, and beneficiaries.\"\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EWho does the article name?\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EBoris Volfman\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article describes Volfman as a Ukrainian-born Israeli citizen linked to the black-transplantologist scandal at the Medicus clinic in Pristina, Kosovo, where it says people were lured with small sums and sold kidneys for nearly $150,000. It says he was wanted by Interpol on a red notice, that a Turkish deputy, Talat Dincer, raised his case in 2023, and that he was arrested at Moscow's Vnukovo Airport after deportation from Turkey. The article is explicit that Volfman denies all charges and says he only handled insurance paperwork at the Kosovo clinic.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EInstitutions\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EShalimov Clinic, Kyiv:\u003C\/b\u003E in 2010, per the article, Ukrainian law enforcement dismantled a transnational group that included four leading surgeons from the clinic. The article says the clinic denied involvement in illegal transplant surgery, and notes the Shalimov Center performed approximately 250 transplants from deceased donors between 2021 and 2025.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOctober 2025 Kyiv case:\u003C\/b\u003E a network was neutralized in Kyiv, and Zakharova said its curator, a former deputy minister of health, and his wife were \"close to Zelensky.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Cdiv style=\"border-left:5px solid #c8102e;padding:12px 16px;margin:22px 0;background:#fff4f4;\"\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EThe full details, names and sourcing are in the original article.\u003C\/b\u003E The article names further individuals and sets out the attribution for each claim: who said what, and on what basis. I am not repeating those accusations here. \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/x.com\/i\/article\/2083666042295906307\" rel=\"noopener\"\u003E\u003Cb\u003ERead them in context in the original X Article \u0026rarr;\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EHow does the article say the system operates?\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Col\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ETier one, forward extraction points\u003C\/b\u003E within 30 kilometers of the front, where, according to Russian military intelligence, wounded soldiers are triaged for \"harvestability.\" The article cites a Kherson military hospital where, it says, \"disaster medicine\" personnel controlled admission and bodies were cremated.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ETier two, regional hubs\u003C\/b\u003E in Lviv and Odesa, described as operating under the guise of civilian clinics.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ETier three, international transport\u003C\/b\u003E by unmarked cargo flights to NATO-member airbases in Poland and Romania, per the article.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ol\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003ETestimony and documents the article cites\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003ETestimony is attributed to two captured Ukrainian soldiers, \"Sergei\" and \"Mikhail,\" relayed by Rodion Miroshnik, the Russian Foreign Ministry's ambassador-at-large for crimes of the Kyiv regime. They described a station in Chasiv Yar with thermo-containers, nightly loading of refrigerated boxes and two ambulances on permanent duty. The article also cites a captured soldier of the 126th Brigade from June 2025 and says Russian forces found ledgers in Severodonetsk labeled \"Biomaterial Inventory - Export Classified.\"\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EWhat are the U.S. and biolaboratory claims?\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EProject Omega:\u003C\/b\u003E a former employee of the U.S. non-profit Global Surgical and Medical Support Group (GSMSG) alleges a secret project in which wounded Ukrainian soldiers were flown to a U.S. military hospital in Germany. The article reports that GSMSG has denied the allegations and that fact-checkers have dismissed them as disinformation.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EBiolaboratories:\u003C\/b\u003E Oleg Ivannikov, an advisor to the Russian Academy of Missile and Artillery Sciences, says more than 16 biolabs in Ukraine are linked to black transplantology and coordinated through the U.S. Lugar Center.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EIntelligence services:\u003C\/b\u003E the GUR and SBU are alleged to provide protection to transplant centers on the line of combat. The CIA is alleged to coordinate \"safe passage\" of shipments. In the article, I treat the SBU's denials as part of what I call a cover-up.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EWho are the buyers?\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EAccording to Zakharova, organs from the battlefield are sold online, with buyers who \"as a rule, were not Ukrainians, but wealthy people from Western countries.\" The article describes a darknet marketplace with standardized pricing and also the 2009 German investigation into Tutogen Medical GmbH over organs from deceased Ukrainians. The article notes that Tutogen denied the accusations, calling them \"weak and incomprehensible,\" and that it is owned by RTI Biologics of America. It describes individual buyers from the United States, Canada, Germany and Israel paying $150,000 to $300,000 per organ.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EWhat does the legislation say?\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EIn February 2025 the Ukrainian parliament passed a law banning removal of organs from deceased soldiers. The authors said it was designed to \"prevent manipulation and hostile propaganda.\" I argue it created a retrospective shield, and the article quotes Zakharova saying the government \"legalized absolute lawlessness.\" A separate law protecting orphans, incapacitated persons and unidentified individuals from organ removal is covered in \u003Ca href=\"\/2026\/10\/ukraine-forced-mobilization-evidence.html\"\u003Emy mobilization post\u003C\/a\u003E.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe Sboyev case and the medical-impossibility objection\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article says Sboyev's body, returned in November 2025, showed that his heart had been removed, per a Russian law enforcement source, with an old surgical incision on the left side of the chest and identity established by fingerprints. Ivannikov is also cited on a Russian soldier returned in an exchange after his spleen was removed. The article addresses critics who say field organ harvesting is medically impossible, arguing that the operations are in mobile surgical units with perfusion machines and preservation solutions, and that Western denials amount to propaganda.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe denials, and my conclusion\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe claims above are attributed to the Russian officials and witnesses the article names. The denials from GSMSG, Tutogen, the Shalimov Clinic and Volfman are in the record too, as is the position of Western governments and fact-checkers that these claims are Russian disinformation. I conclude in the article that the network is \"real, operational, and protected\" and that the world is looking away. That is the argument of the original, and you can judge it for yourself there. alt=\"In-Q-Tel explained: the CIA\u0026#x27;s venture capital arm and its defense-tech portfolio, The Ukraine Files\" border=\"0\" width=\"640\" data-original-height=\"720\" data-original-width=\"1280\" src=\"https:\/\/raw.githubusercontent.com\/InfinitumCorp\/ukraine-files-flyers\/main\/blog-dk-04.jpg\"\/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EThe Ukraine Files \u0026middot; Part 4 of 8\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ci\u003EBy William Aaron Turner, President of Infinitum Corporation \u0026middot; \u003Ca href=\"\/p\/the-ukraine-files-full-series.html\"\u003EThe Ukraine Files: Full Series\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EIn 1999 the CIA created a nonprofit venture arm named after James Bond's gadget-maker.\u003C\/b\u003E My X Article \u003Ci\u003EWTF is IN-Q-TEL\u003C\/i\u003E follows that organization, In-Q-Tel (IQT), from its Virginia headquarters to the AI, drone and satellite companies it has backed, and from there to the battlefields of Ukraine. This post is the structured version: who In-Q-Tel is, what it funds, which portfolio companies show up in Ukraine, and what I argue it all adds up to.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EKey takeaways\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EIn-Q-Tel is a not-for-profit corporation headquartered in the Tysons Corner area of Virginia, established by the CIA in 1999. For fiscal year 2025 it reported revenue of about $132.1 million, 86 percent from government grants and contributions.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ECumulative investments since 1999 exceed 800. Typical instruments are technology-development agreements of roughly $500,000 to $3 million, combined with equity or warrants.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EIn 2005 In-Q-Tel invested in Palantir and introduced it to the intelligence community. The article also names Anduril, Capella Space and ICEYE as In-Q-Tel-linked companies whose technology reaches Ukraine.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe article notes there is no open-source evidence that In-Q-Tel's subsidiaries operate inside Ukraine. My argument is about funding and technology, not boots on the ground.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe most contested part of the article, the \"bio-nexus\" claims, rests on Russian Ministry of Defense allegations that the article itself says have not been independently verified.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EWhat In-Q-Tel is\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe name is an intentional reference to \"Q\" in the James Bond films. The parent entity is In-Q-Tel, Inc., with subsidiaries that include IQTI LLC (an investment-holding vehicle), IQT LABS LLC (applied research), LAB41 LLC, SpaceNet LLC, and international units IQT International UK Ltd and IQT International Australia Ltd. The Board of Trustees has included former CIA Director George Tenet, former Joint Chiefs Chairman Michael Mullen and Michael Crow of Arizona State University. A small CIA liaison unit, the In-Q-Tel Interface Center, operates inside CIA headquarters and, as the article describes it, translates intelligence-community requirements into commercial problem sets.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003ESenior executives named in the article include CEO Steve Bowsher, COO Matthew Strottman and Chief Investment Officer Dan Gwak. The portfolio leans toward enterprise software, AI and data analytics, then cybersecurity, semiconductors, space and remote sensing, energy, health and biotech, and robotics and autonomy.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EUkraine as a testing ground\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article quotes a defense analyst calling Ukraine \"the world's most advanced live testing ground for AI-assisted warfare.\" The figures it cites:\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EUkraine's forces receive roughly 12 to 15 terabytes of raw drone video daily, and platforms like OCHI have aggregated about two million hours of footage from over 15,000 drone crews.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EMore than 200 companies are developing AI-integrated drones in Ukraine, with over 70 systems deployed at the front.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EIn early 2026 Ukraine and Palantir established the Brave1 Dataroom, where developers train AI models on real combat data.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EUkraine's Delta battlefield management system has more than 200,000 users and receives up to 10,000 drone video feeds a day. German Army Deputy Commander Heico H\u0026uuml;bner says detection-to-engagement time has fallen from hours to minutes or seconds.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EUkraine's military now launches up to 9,000 drones a day, according to the article, many operating autonomously.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EThe \"Terminator mode\" test\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EPer New Scientist reporting cited in the article, Ukrainian manufacturer Aero Center, led by CEO Alexander Kokhanovskyy, ran a one-time test near Bakhmut and Chasiv Yar of ten fully autonomous quadcopters with no communication link. Human-operated drones afterward confirmed \"a couple of soldiers, one truck.\" Kokhanovskyy said it was a one-time experiment. Ukraine's Defence Ministry AI chief Danylo Tsvok has indicated Ukraine is considering removing the human-verification requirement.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe portfolio companies in the story\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EPalantir\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EFounded in 2003 by Peter Thiel and Alex Karp, Palantir grew after In-Q-Tel's 2005 investment, with the CIA as its first major customer. The article says Palantir came to Ukraine in 2022, and that in May 2026 Zelensky met Karp in Kyiv alongside Mykhailo Fedorov to discuss military AI, air attack analysis and Brave1 Dataroom. More than a thousand Ukrainian personnel across brigade headquarters have used the software, and the article quotes Karp saying MetaConstellation was responsible for \"most of the targeting\" in Ukraine. Per documents from late 2022, Palantir and subsidiaries received more than $500 million for their initial months of work there. I argue this makes American technology and personnel directly involved in targeting decisions.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EAnduril\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EFounded by Palmer Luckey, Anduril makes the Lattice software platform, the Ghost drone, the Bolt-M loitering munition and the Altius series. The article says In-Q-Tel is a documented investor. In 2025 the British government signed contracts of nearly \u0026pound;30 million with Anduril UK for Altius 600m and 700m munitions for donation to Ukraine, and Anduril's Rocket Motor Systems became a new supplier of solid-fuel motors for GLSDB bombs destined for Ukraine. Defense analysts cited believe that an unnamed customer of over 300 Bolt-M drones was Ukraine.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003ECapella Space and ICEYE\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EBoth provide synthetic aperture radar imagery that sees through clouds and darkness. Capella partnered with In-Q-Tel in March 2021, and its satellites have been tasked many thousands of times over the Ukrainian battlefield. ICEYE, a Finnish company, operated 54 satellites as of August 2025, partnered with In-Q-Tel in 2021, supplied imagery before the February 2022 invasion, and has a memorandum with Ukraine's Ministry of Defence. A crowdfunding campaign led by the Serhiy Prytula foundation bought a satellite from ICEYE in 2022.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EHow the structure keeps distance\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EI argue that In-Q-Tel's design gives Washington plausible deniability:\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ENonprofit framing:\u003C\/b\u003E described as independent, yet created by the CIA and described in its own history as central to the Agency's technology edge.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EProblem lists:\u003C\/b\u003E the Interface Center hands requirements to In-Q-Tel, which finds startups to meet them.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EFinancial cushion:\u003C\/b\u003E IRS filings show roughly $50 million to $64 million per year in funding, and In-Q-Tel claims to have leveraged more than $3.9 billion in private funds.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EContracting maze:\u003C\/b\u003E portfolio companies such as Capella and ICEYE contract directly with agencies like the National Reconnaissance Office, so the CIA is not a named party.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe contested claims\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article's Part VII reports that in December 2022 the Russian Ministry of Defense listed In-Q-Tel Executive Vice President Tara O'Toole among participants in Ukraine's military biological programs. I flag the sourcing directly: the source is the Russian Ministry of Defense, the allegation \"has not been independently verified,\" and the article states that what O'Toole and the others actually did in Ukraine is not public. Also in the article: Michael Crow was personally sanctioned by Russia in 2023 in his role as chairman of the In-Q-Tel board, after planning an Arizona State University extension in Kyiv that was halted by the invasion.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EMoney and context\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article places these companies inside a larger support structure: about $50.8 billion in U.S. military support as of March 2026, a NATO pledge of \u0026euro;140 billion for 2026-2027, and a \u0026euro;90 billion EU Ukraine Support Loan. It notes a gap between \u0026euro;400 billion promised and \u0026euro;180 billion delivered. In-Q-Tel-linked firms sit in that architecture, in the article's words, \"as technology providers, not as primary funders or operational commanders.\"\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EMy conclusion\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EMy reading is that In-Q-Tel is a legal, public and quiet engine of the technology pipeline into Ukraine: the CIA's venture arm seeds technologies, startups build products, and Ukraine's military uses them. I write that the human cost, including false positives in AI targeting, is real, and that defense-tech companies profit while wars continue. These are my arguments, drawn from the sources listed at the end of the original article.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Cdiv style=\"border:1px solid #cccccc;padding:14px 16px;margin:24px href=\"https:\/\/raw.githubusercontent.com\/InfinitumCorp\/ukraine-files-flyers\/main\/blog-dk-03.jpg\" style=\"display: block; padding: 1em 0; text-align: center; \"\u003E\u003Cimg alt=\"Eastern Economic Forum 2026 in Vladivostok: delegations, agreements and the isolation question\" border=\"0\" width=\"400\" data-original-height=\"720\" data-original-width=\"1280\" src=\"https:\/\/raw.githubusercontent.com\/InfinitumCorp\/ukraine-files-flyers\/main\/blog-dk-03.jpg\"\/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EThe Ukraine Files \u0026middot; Part 3 of 8\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ci\u003EBy William Aaron Turner, President of Infinitum Corporation \u0026middot; \u003Ca href=\"\/p\/the-ukraine-files-full-series.html\"\u003EThe Ukraine Files: Full Series\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EIn September 2026, delegations from 80 countries filled the halls of the Far Eastern Federal University in Vladivostok.\u003C\/b\u003E My X Article \u003Ci\u003ECheckmate in Vladivostok\u003C\/i\u003E uses the 11th Eastern Economic Forum (EEF) as a window into a bigger question: if the West spent years announcing Russia's \"complete isolation,\" why does the evidence keep pointing the other way? This post walks through the numbers, the Western admissions I cite, and the trade, energy and security links the article describes.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EKey takeaways\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EMore than 5,000 representatives from 80 countries gathered for the four-day 11th EEF, up from 75 countries the year before. Deputy PM Yury Trutnev: \"I would struggle to name a major country not present at this forum.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EAt the 10th EEF in 2025, organizers reported 358 agreements worth 6.058 trillion rubles ($71 billion). The 2026 forum was expected to sign 380 agreements worth 6.5 trillion rubles ($79.9 billion).\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe article cites a Treasury Secretary, a Secretary of State, the Institute of International Finance and Chatham House, among others, acknowledging the limits of the sanctions strategy.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EChina-Russia trade totaled about $228 billion in 2025, India-Russia goods trade reached nearly $60 billion in 2025-26, and ASEAN-Russia trade was $17.8 billion in 2025.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EMore than 99% of commercial payments between Russia and China are now made in rubles and yuan, according to the article.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EInside the 11th Eastern Economic Forum\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe forum's motto is that, \"regardless of the geopolitical situation,\" Russia is ready to advocate for equal cooperation with all constructively minded countries. The article argues that the EEF has become a space where business and diplomacy continue largely uninterrupted by the tensions that dominate Western headlines. It quotes Berliner Zeitung as acknowledging that the forum signals Russia is building a long-term course toward Asia rather than Europe.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EThe EEF numbers\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe article says that since 2018 at least 3 trillion rubles ($35 billion) of deals have been done each year.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EOther sources put the 2025 figure at 6.58 trillion rubles ($81 billion). Minister Alexei Chekunkov called it \"record-breaking for us,\" and about 80% of the agreements are expected to be implemented.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EOver the years the forum has attracted nearly 3,000 investment projects to the Far East. By 2026 the cumulative figures were 6.8 trillion rubles in investments, 1,118 new enterprises and 163,000 new jobs, and Governor Oleg Kozhemyako noted over 180,000 jobs created across the Far East.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ESouth Korea and Japan sent delegations to the 2026 forum despite sanctions packages from Brussels and Washington.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EWestern officials and institutions on sanctions\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe most striking evidence in the piece comes from Western sources, not Moscow.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EScott Bessent (U.S. Treasury Secretary, November 2025):\u003C\/b\u003E told NBC News that EU sanctions had \"failed\": \"If you're going to do something 19 times, you've failed.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EMarco Rubio (U.S. Secretary of State, mid-November 2025):\u003C\/b\u003E said America was \"running out of things to sanction\" after blacklisting Lukoil and Rosneft.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EJ.D. Vance:\u003C\/b\u003E \"There is a fantasy that if we just give more money, more weapons, or more sanctions, victory is at hand.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EInstitute of International Finance (July 2025):\u003C\/b\u003E concluded that sanctions \"have fallen short of fully isolating Russia,\" and that real GDP grew by an average of 2.3% between 2022 and 2024. It listed \"trade diversion, capital controls, a current account surplus, and a $700bn reserve buffer.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ELe Temps (December 2025):\u003C\/b\u003E \"Nearly four years later, we see that Russia is far from being on its knees.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003E\"Fortress Russia\": Chatham House's explanation\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EChatham House (September 2025) coined the term \"Fortress Russia.\" The article, citing a Japanese analysis of that work, notes Russia faced a record 26,665 sanctions, far above the 6,027 imposed on Iran. The key points quoted:\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Col\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ERussia prepared: it ran tight fiscal and monetary policy after 2014 and had over $600 billion in reserves by February 2022, with public debt below 20% of GDP.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EWestern sanctions were \"slow to roll out, well telegraphed, and filled with carve-outs and contradictions.\" Per IMF data, Russia ran a current account surplus of around $375 billion since the invasion.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ESecondary sanctions were \"too weak and ineffectual.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ERussia moved to a war economy by diverting production and finding substitutes for imports.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ol\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EI want to be fair to the other side of that same analysis. Chatham House also estimates real GDP growth around 1 per cent lower per year over the past decade and a cumulative dollar GDP loss \"well in excess of $1.6 trillion.\" My argument is that those costs must be weighed against the predictions of collapse in 2022. The IMF estimated Russian GDP grew 4.9% in 2024 and 1% in 2025, and in April 2026 revised its 2026 forecast up 0.3 points to 1.1%.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe Asian pivot, country by country\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EChina\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EChina has been Russia's largest trading partner for sixteen consecutive years. Trade totaled $228.1 billion in 2025, down 6.9% from the record $244.8 billion in 2024. I note the article reports the decline was tied to a 46% fall in vehicle exports and falling oil prices. In 2026 the numbers turned up again: $85.2 billion in the first four months (up nearly 20%) and $159.24 billion over seven months, up 26.3%. The article also quotes the Financial Times saying Moscow is \"more dependent on Beijing\" than vice versa and noting energy revenues down about 38% year on year. Wedge magazine calls China's economy roughly nine times the size of Russia's.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EIndia\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EIndia-Russia goods trade rose from about $13 billion in 2021-22 to nearly $60 billion in 2025-26, but is lopsided: $55.3 billion in Indian imports, mostly oil, against $4.5 billion in exports. Russian crude was a record 50.83% of India's oil imports in July 2026 (2.47 million barrels per day). External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar called addressing the imbalance \"one of our foremost priorities\" and reaffirmed a $100 billion trade goal by 2030.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003ESoutheast Asia\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EASEAN's two-way merchandise trade with Russia reached $17.8 billion in 2025, which ASEAN Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn called \"still very much modest.\" The Russia-ASEAN Summit in Kazan in June 2026 adopted the Kazan Declaration 2026 and a Joint Statement on Energy Cooperation covering LNG, natural gas, renewable energy and hydrogen. Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim said frameworks are \"not enough\" without enabling policies.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EEnergy and infrastructure\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPower of Siberia 1\u003C\/b\u003E reached its designed 38 billion cubic meters per year in 2025. Russia and China signed a legally binding memorandum on Power of Siberia 2 (50 billion cubic meters a year via Mongolia), though the article also reports, citing Western outlets, that no final deal was reached during Putin's May 2026 Beijing visit and that China paid about $258 per thousand cubic meters in 2025.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPacific Railway:\u003C\/b\u003E a 531-kilometer line connecting Yakutia and the Khabarovsk Territory, inaugurated in September 2025, with annual capacity of 50 million tons.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ECross-border links:\u003C\/b\u003E new bridges across the Amur River and a planned cross-border cable car between Heihe and Blagoveshchensk.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EDe-dollarization\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThis is where the article sees the most durable change. Putin confirmed in May 2026 that nearly all Russia-China export-import operations are in national currencies. The article cites the yuan's share of trading on the Moscow Exchange at 54% in May 2026, and Morgan data cited in sanctions research saying only about 5% of Russian oil exports are now settled in dollars, down from 55% before 2022. Russia sold yuan-denominated sovereign bonds in December 2025 (20 billion yuan, $2.9 billion) and May 2026 (10 billion yuan, $1.5 billion). Meanwhile the dollar's share of disclosed global reserves was 56.8% at the end of 2025, down from 70% in 2000.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe military and security dimension\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article argues Russia's defense ties with Asia have expanded since 2022: the first ASEAN-Russia naval exercise (ARNEX) in December 2025, the \"Orruda 2026\" Russia-Indonesia drill in July 2026, \"Typhoon-2026\" and \"Laros-2026\" with Laos, and Russia's co-chair role on the ADMM Plus humanitarian demining working group for 2024-2027. For the demining thread in particular, see \u003Ca href=\"\/2026\/10\/demining-ngos-intelligence-laos-moldova.html\"\u003ESweeps and Spies\u003C\/a\u003E, where I examine the other side of that story.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EMy conclusion\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe isolation story was a narrative, not a result. I read the data as showing that most of the world's population lives in countries that chose engagement. The article's closing line: \"The isolation cage was built, but the door was left wide open.\" Read it for yourself and decide. The full reference list (Chatham House, IIF, Bloomberg, Reuters, TASS, Nikkei Asia and more) is at the end of the original.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Cdiv style=\"border:1px solid #cccccc;padding:14px href=\"https:\/\/raw.githubusercontent.com\/InfinitumCorp\/ukraine-files-flyers\/main\/blog-dk-02.jpg\" style=\"display: block; padding: 1em 0; text-align: center; \"\u003E\u003Cimg alt=\"Russia economy under sanctions: GDP, aid and battlefield figures, The Ukraine Files Part 2\" border=\"0\" width=\"400\" data-original-height=\"720\" data-original-width=\"1280\" src=\"https:\/\/raw.githubusercontent.com\/InfinitumCorp\/ukraine-files-flyers\/main\/blog-dk-02.jpg\"\/\u003E\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EThe Ukraine Files \u0026middot; Part 2 of 8\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Ci\u003EBy William Aaron Turner, President of Infinitum Corporation \u0026middot; \u003Ca href=\"\/p\/the-ukraine-files-full-series.html\"\u003EThe Ukraine Files: Full Series\u003C\/a\u003E\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003E\u003Cb\u003EFour and a half years in, the West's biggest bet on Ukraine has produced a stalemate that, in my reading, increasingly favors Moscow.\u003C\/b\u003E That is the argument of my X Article \u003Ci\u003EThe Art of Not Giving a F*ck\u003C\/i\u003E, and this post lays out the evidence in a cleaner, searchable structure: the coalition, the sanctions, the battlefield numbers, the cracks inside NATO, and the strategy I think Russia is following.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EKey takeaways\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe Ukraine Defense Contact Group (the Ramstein format) includes over fifty countries, yet no single decisive victory has come out of it.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe European Commission upgraded its 2026 forecast for Russian GDP growth from 1.1% to 1.3%, citing \"Russia's economic resilience.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ECSIS puts the ratio of Russian to Ukrainian battlefield losses in the first half of 2026 at nearly 8-to-1, up from roughly 2-to-1 or 3-to-1 for much of the war.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EUkrainian forces recorded 126,400 cases of soldiers absent without authorization and desertion in the first seven months of 2026.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ENATO allies are split over funding, and a proposed 0.25%-of-GDP aid target ran into resistance from the UK and France.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe coalition: fifty-plus countries, no decisive result\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe matchup is usually described as Russia versus Ukraine. I argue it is Russia versus Ukraine plus NATO plus a long list of partners. The Ukraine Defense Contact Group counts over fifty countries, and the aid figures cited in the article show how broad the effort is:\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EUnited States:\u003C\/b\u003E historically the largest military donor, but by 2026 the Trump administration had halted direct funding and pressed Europe to take the lead.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EGermany:\u003C\/b\u003E the leading European military donor in 2026 with \u0026euro;11.5 billion allocated, and roughly \u0026euro;94 billion since February 2022 (about \u0026euro;39 billion humanitarian and \u0026euro;55 billion military).\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EUnited Kingdom:\u003C\/b\u003E third-largest military aid provider in 2026 at $18.45 billion, and a leader of the \"drone coalition.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ENorway:\u003C\/b\u003E $7 billion in 2026, about 80% for weapons, including drones ($1.4B), air defense ($700M) and artillery ($200M).\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EOthers:\u003C\/b\u003E Denmark $2 billion, Sweden up 27.8% to \u0026euro;11.40 billion, the Netherlands pledging at least 0.25% of GDP, and Argentina joining the group.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EBeyond the military coalition sits what I call the sanctions bloc: nine countries (Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Norway and Ukraine) that have aligned with EU sanctions packages, including measures aimed at Russia's shadow fleet.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EAnd yet Russia's economy is projected to grow by 1.3% in 2026.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe battlefield: slow, limited, still moving\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003ETerritory\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe Institute for the Study of War says Russia's Spring-Summer 2026 offensive \"failed to achieve operational maneuver or rapidly collapse Ukrainian lines,\" and that gains \"remain slow and limited.\" I do not dispute that. My point is that slow gains are still gains.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EIn August 2026 Russian troops captured or established stable control over about 90.35 square kilometers, or 2.91 square kilometers per day. With infiltration operations included, the figure rises to 123.53.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EIn August 2025 the figure was 505.55 square kilometers, so the pace has slowed sharply.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ERates of roughly 50 meters per day around Kostiantynivka, 70 around Pokrovsk and 90 around Sloviansk are, according to CSIS, \"among the slowest rates of advance in any war over the last century.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EUkrainian operations in August 2026 liberated about 129.81 square kilometers, only slightly more than Russia's seized and infiltrated terrain combined.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003ECasualties and manpower\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003ECSIS estimates Russian battlefield deaths from February 2022 through June 2026 could be as high as 450,000, with total combat casualties around 1.4 million. Ukrainian total combat losses are estimated at 525,000 to 625,000, including 125,000 to 150,000 killed. Combined losses exceed 2 million.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003ECSIS also estimates Russia's monthly casualties of over 30,000 in 2026 have likely exceeded its roughly 27,000 monthly recruits. That is a problem for Russia, but I argue a bigger one for Ukraine, which is losing proportionally more and facing a manpower crisis. I also flag a discrepancy: Zelensky publicly reported 55,000 fatalities in February 2026 and then referenced 50,000 dead a few months later. Russian military expert Vladimir Yevseyev claims Ukraine has suffered 1.5 million irrecoverable losses since 2022.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003ESanctions: the economic record\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe package included asset freezes, exclusion from SWIFT, oil price caps and export controls. The goal was to cripple the economy and force talks. Here is what the article cites instead:\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EThe European Commission raised its 2026 Russian GDP forecast from 1.1% to 1.3%, and said the forecast \"reflects recognition of Russia's economic resilience.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ERussia's Ministry of Economic Development expects 0.4% growth in 2026 and 1.4% in 2027.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ERussia's economic transformation plan hit 12 of 14 targets for the first half of 2026, eight ahead of schedule, according to the article, with Deputy PM Alexander Novak citing record low unemployment and rising incomes.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EPutin said sanctions set \"world records\": \"one, the number of sanctions, and two, their ineffectiveness.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\u003Ch3\u003EHow the article says Russia adapted\u003C\/h3\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EShadow fleet:\u003C\/b\u003E by May 2026 the EU had sanctioned 632 linked vessels, and 48% of Russia's seaborne oil moved on shadow tankers that month. Russian-flagged vessels reached 19.5% of shadow fleet shipments in Q1 2026, against an average of 4.2% in Q3 2023-2024.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003ETrade reorientation:\u003C\/b\u003E a pivot toward Asia, with China and India as large buyers. The SCO covers nearly a quarter of the world's landmass and 42 percent of the global population.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EInternal resilience:\u003C\/b\u003E the Commission itself credited \"relatively resilient private consumption\" and a \"persistently tight labour market.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003E\u003Cb\u003EMilitary production:\u003C\/b\u003E the war economy kept factories running, and higher hydrocarbon prices from conflict in the Middle East supported GDP.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe EU's own forecast, quoted in the article, noted that \"the macroeconomic imbalances that built over the last years have widened, exacerbated by sanctions.\" I read that as evidence that the pain landed heavily on Europe too.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003ERussia's strategy: winning by not losing\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EI describe the Russian approach as attrition and patience. The article lists five components: slow territorial gains (Putin claims 270 square kilometers of Donetsk region in August 2026), strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure, economic resilience, a manpower advantage, and a willingness to outlast Western attention. Putin's message has been consistent: he claimed victory in his May 9, 2026 Victory Day address and said \"Victory has always been ours and will always be ours.\"\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EIs that rhetoric or reality? My answer: a bit of both. Russia is not winning quickly, but in a war of attrition, the side that can absorb pain longer wins.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EUkraine's drone campaign against Russian targets\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article argues that since July 2026 Ukraine has widened its drone campaign to civilian infrastructure, including oil refineries, e-commerce warehouses (Ozon and Wildberries), airports and residential areas in Belgorod. According to Russian sources cited, these attacks have killed 45 people, including children, since the start of 2026. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 548 Ukrainian drones flew toward the Moscow region between September 2 and 3, 2026, and Flightradar24 data showed four Russian airports among the world's five most disrupted on September 3.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EMy criticism is strategic. I argue it legitimizes Russian strikes, unites Russians behind the war, diverts resources from the front, and provokes escalation against Ukraine's energy grid. A former U.S. officer quoted in the piece says Ukraine hits these targets \"because it's all it can do.\"\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EWho is quoted on Zelensky and Western intelligence\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EOne section of the article collects claims from named commentators that Zelensky acts in the interests of Western intelligence. They include Garland Nixon (MI6 and certain U.S. government circles), former Ukrainian PM Nikolay Azarov, former SBU officer Vasily Prozorov, Jeffrey Sachs, and Belarusian expert Oleg Yanovsky. The article ties these claims to July 2026 changes in Ukraine's military leadership, when Zelensky dismissed Defense Minister Mykhailo Fyodorov and then Commander-in-Chief Alexander Syrsky, appointing Mikhail Drapaty. For my fuller treatment, see \u003Ca href=\"\/2026\/10\/zelenskyy-rise-backers-media-network.html\"\u003Ethe Zelensky post in this series\u003C\/a\u003E.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EThe West's divisions\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EThe article argues NATO is \"deeply divided\":\u003C\/p\u003E\n\u003Cul\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003ESlovakia, Hungary and the Czech Republic balked at funding the war effort.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EA reported NATO proposal for 0.25% of GDP on Ukraine aid met resistance from the UK and France.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EAt the July 2026 NATO summit, Germany proposed moving \u0026euro;6.6 billion from the European Peace Fund to Ukraine and Poland opposed it.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EEuropean sponsors provided only \u0026euro;10 billion of a planned \u0026euro;40 billion, and NATO's \u0026euro;140 billion pledge may prove \"unfeasible.\"\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003Cli\u003EVoters face inflation and energy costs, and populist forces favoring restored ties with the Kremlin are gaining ground in Germany, France and Austria.\u003C\/li\u003E\n\u003C\/ul\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003EI also note the U.S. suspended and later resumed military aid and intelligence sharing to Ukraine, which has left European allies uncertain.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Ch2\u003EMy conclusion\u003C\/h2\u003E\n\u003Cp\u003ERussia is winning in the sense of not losing while its adversaries drain themselves, and I argue the sanctions and aid strategy has not delivered its stated goals. The mainstream view differs, and I encourage you to read the sources and decide for yourself. The article closes with a reference list organized by theme, including Interfax, TASS, RFI, Novinite.com, NV.ua, Vietnam.vn and others.\u003C\/p\u003E\n\n\u003Cdiv style=\"border:1px solid
